paper_title: Continual Dialogue State Tracking via Reason-of-Select Distillation
caption: : Error rate for slots
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of error rates across various dialogue slots, as reported in the paper “Continual Dialogue State Tracking via Reason-of-Select Distillation.” It is composed of 15 distinct segments, each representing a different slot type with its corresponding error percentage. The largest segment is “date,” accounting for 19.30% of the total error, followed by “from” at 17.00%, “to” at 14.50%, and “genre” at 13.50%. Smaller segments include “name” (5.20%), “size” (4.20%), “time” (4.10%), “intent” and “location” (both 3.80%), “destination” (3.00%), “city” (2.60%), “class” (2.40%), “range” (2.20%), “type” (2.00%), “beds” (1.30%), and “passengers” (1.10%). Each slice is color-coded and labeled with its slot name and percentage, and the segments are arranged radially in descending order of magnitude, starting from the top-right and moving clockwise. No legend is present, as labels are directly attached to each slice. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of temporal and destination-related slots in contributing to overall dialogue state tracking errors.
